extracted.intended_audience: writers, students, and scholars of literature and art
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and conceptual criteria for using defamiliarization (ostranenie) as an artistic technique to make the familiar strange across language, narrative, and other artistic forms so readers gain new perceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Present ordinary things in an unfamiliar way
rubrics_metrics.description: The artistic technique of presenting common or ordinary things in an unfamiliar or strange way so audiences can gain new perspectives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the core definition: make objects, events, language, or situations seem unfamiliar (ostranenie) to renew perception; used across art and poetry to force new ways of seeing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Increase difficulty and length of perception
rubrics_metrics.description: Make forms difficult and increase the difficulty and length of perception because the process of perception is an aesthetic end in itself and must be prolonged.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Shklovsky: the technique of art is to make objects 'unfamiliar' to prolong perception. Practically, slow readers' automatic comprehension to make them notice details and produce aesthetic effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prevent automatization / create deautomatized perception
rubrics_metrics.description: Remove the automatism of perception so the audience does not 'function as though by formula' and instead experiences renewed perceptual awareness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The author's purpose is to create the vision which results from deautomatized perception; a work is created 'artistically' so that perception is impeded and maximum effect is produced through slowness of perception.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish poetic from practical language (use 'formed speech')
rubrics_metrics.description: Poetic speech is 'formed speech' distinct from ordinary, economical prose; poetic language should be perceptible and less immediately 'easy' than practical language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Shklovsky’s distinction suggests using language that resists facile comprehension: choices in diction, syntax, and rhythm should highlight artfulness rather than mimic everyday speech.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manipulate phonetic and lexical structures
rubrics_metrics.description: Use phonetic/lexical structure and characteristic distributions of words to reveal artistic 'trademarks' that remove automatism of perception.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examine sound, word choice, word-order, and collocation to make language itself noticeable; the page emphasizes study of phonetic and lexical elements as tools for defamiliarization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use unfamiliar narrative point of view
rubrics_metrics.description: Adopt a nonstandard narrator or perspective (e.g., a horse narrator in Tolstoy's 'Kholstomer') to make ordinary content seem strange.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Changing the perceiver (who tells the story) alters what is familiar; nonhuman or unexpected narrators foreground assumptions and thereby defamiliarize events and objects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Employ foreign language, dialect, or 'barbarisms'
rubrics_metrics.description: Introduce foreign languages, dialects, or colloquialisms to disrupt normalized literary language and create estrangement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Shklovsky notes shifts from literary language to colloquial/dialect forms and the converse; deliberately inserting nonstandard registers draws attention to language and cultural assumptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Defamiliarize plot by manipulating syuzhet vs fabula
rubrics_metrics.description: Transform the fabula (basic story material) into an unfamiliar syuzhet (plot formation) through ordering and presentation choices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Techniques include temporal displacements, digressions, causal disruptions, and placing effects before causes (e.g., Sterne's Tristram Shandy) to slow readers’ ability to reassemble the familiar story.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use temporal displacements, digressions, and causal disruption
rubrics_metrics.description: Employ narrative strategies that dislocate time and causality so the reader's habitual reconstruction of events is impeded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical methods: non-linear chronology, frequent digressions, and disrupting cause–effect expectations to force readers to re-evaluate narrative meaning and notice form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Produce estrangement (Verfremdungseffekt) or recontextualization
rubrics_metrics.description: Create an estrangement effect—making the familiar appear strange—either via defamiliarization or deliberate recontextualization of familiar elements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Related but distinct concepts: Brecht's Verfremdungseffekt is an effect on the audience (often political/theatrical), while defamiliarization is a formal-rhetorical device; both aim to prevent passive consumption and promote critical perception.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evoke the uncanny by blending strange and familiar
rubrics_metrics.description: Situate strange elements within a quotidian frame (or vice versa) to produce an uncanny feeling in which the familiar becomes unsettling.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Freud’s uncanny: not fear of unknown but a return to long-familiar material rendered strange; writers can present supernatural or odd elements as if in ordinary reality to provoke uncertainty and unease.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alter perception in ways analogous to Derrida’s différance
rubrics_metrics.description: Defamiliarization both 'differs' and 'defers'—it alters perception and forces readers to think about concepts in different, often more complex, terms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Theoretical framing: defamiliarization creates difference and temporal/interpretive deferment, producing new value and motion in perception; useful as a conceptual justification for strategies that delay comprehension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apply defamiliarization across genres, media, and movements
rubrics_metrics.description: The technique is applicable in multiple artistic movements (Dadaism, postmodernism, epic theatre, science fiction) and tactics (e.g., culture jamming).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical implication: defamiliarization is not limited to poetry—use it in theater, film, prose, speculative fiction, and activist art; methods will vary by medium but share the aim of renewing perception.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make artistic choices visible to the reader
rubrics_metrics.description: Use devices that make readers aware of the artistic procedures causing difficulty of perception.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Margolin: defamiliarization increases awareness of devices and procedures; designers of texts can intentionally foreground rhetorical/artistic operations so the act of reading becomes part of the aesthetic experience.
